evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f requests an Angular latest-version Excel add-in POC.

[fact] The npm registry latest endpoints returned @angular/core 22.1.6 and @angular/cli 22.1.8 at 2026-09-15T15:28:23.9407966Z: https://registry.npmjs.org/@angular/core/latest and https://registry.npmjs.org/@angular/cli/latest.
[fact] Target repository commit cc3cc10e0bef9cebb7fea946709ac9aa9b26354d is clean and has no tracked product files, so there is no existing scaffold or repository convention to preserve.

requirements.text: Expose exactly 10 mocked variables with distinct identifiers, display names, and finite randomly generated numeric values that remain stable for the lifetime of one add-in runtime.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f requests 10 mocked variables and random values.

[inference] Generating values once when the shared runtime initializes makes the POC observable and prevents one variable from changing between task-pane, command, and custom-function reads; a page/runtime reload may generate a new set. This implementation choice can be verified with focused store tests.

requirements.text: When a user selects one contiguous range or multiple discontiguous ranges and clicks a variable in the task pane, write that variable's numeric value into every selected cell.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f explicitly requests click-to-insert for one or multiple selected cells.

[fact] Microsoft documents Workbook.getSelectedRanges() as returning all selected ranges through RangeAreas in ExcelApi 1.9: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/excel/excel.workbook?view=excel-js-preview#getselectedranges.

[fact] Microsoft documents RangeAreas.areas as a RangeCollection whose loaded items are Excel.Range objects; each range exposes rowCount, columnCount, and values: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/excel/excel.rangeareas?view=excel-js-preview and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/excel/excel.rangecollection?view=excel-js-preview.

[inference] A single insertion service can load the selected areas and their dimensions, assign a value matrix to each member range, and synchronize once; tests with mocked Office.js objects can verify single-area, multi-area, and rejected-operation paths.

requirements.text: Add an Excel cell context-menu command named 'Insert selected variable' that writes the currently active mocked variable into every cell in one or multiple selected ranges.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f requests a custom right-click Insert variable command for one or multiple selected cells.

[fact] Microsoft documents an add-in-only manifest ContextMenu extension with OfficeMenu id ContextMenuCell and an ExecuteFunction action: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/manifest/extensionpoint?view=excel-js-preview#contextmenu.

[fact] Microsoft documents that a shared runtime lets Excel task panes, function commands, and custom functions share data in one runtime: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/dev/add-ins/testing/runtimes.

[inference] The task pane should keep one active variable, defaulting to the first mock variable, in a shared state module so the manifest command always has a defined value; the command handler must always complete its Office event and surface failures without leaving an unhandled promise.

requirements.text: Support dragging a variable's DOM element directly from the task pane and dropping it onto a specific Excel worksheet cell or selected worksheet ranges.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f asks to research and implement task-pane-to-cell drag where feasible and to explain impossible scenarios.

[fact] Microsoft documents that task-pane code runs inside a sandboxed browser/webview surface: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/dev/add-ins/overview/office-add-ins and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/dev/add-ins/concepts/browsers-used-by-office-web-add-ins.

[fact] The documented Office DragAndDropEvent and pointer-coordinate payload are Outlook-only and describe messages or attachments dropped into an Outlook task pane, not task-pane objects dropped onto an Excel grid: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/outlook/office.draganddropeventargs?view=outlook-js-preview.

[inference] The published Excel Office.js surface exposes selection and workbook events but no supported cross-webview worksheet drop target, target-cell coordinates, or Excel drag payload for a DOM element. A native task-pane-to-grid drop cannot therefore be implemented reliably as an Office.js POC; an Office/Office.js product capability would be needed to verify otherwise.

requirements.text: Explain the unsupported native drag interaction in the POC and present supported UX alternatives without pretending that a task-pane drag identifies an Excel drop cell.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f requires explanations and UX alternatives for impossible scenarios.
[fact] REQ-003 and REQ-004 identify two supported alternatives: select cells then click a variable, or select an active variable then invoke the Excel cell context-menu command.

[inference] A short in-app note plus README feasibility table is sufficient for the POC; a task-pane-only drag target would add a third interaction but would not satisfy native worksheet drop semantics and is not required.

requirements.text: Provide an add-in-only Excel manifest that targets the local Angular HTTPS origin, grants read/write workbook access, declares ExcelApi 1.9 and SharedRuntime 1.1, loads the task pane, exposes the context-menu action, and declares custom-function resources.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f requires a manifest targeting a local Angular HTTPS app and reuse of the ps-excel-agent manifest pattern.

[fact] ps-excel-agent origin/main c4900f696aeb1af3f78f377a6f61f35e28e1e59f file planningspace.integration.excel.ui/manifest.xml lines 32-104 demonstrates ExcelApi and SharedRuntime requirements, ReadWriteDocument, a long-lived shared runtime, CustomFunctions resources, FunctionFile, and https://localhost:3000 task-pane/function URLs.
[fact] Microsoft recommends HTTPS during Office add-in development and allows trusted development certificates: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/dev/add-ins/tutorials/excel-tutorial.

[inference] The POC should adapt the verified XML structure to Angular's local HTTPS origin (planned as https://localhost:4200) and use ExcelApi 1.9 because discontiguous selection depends on getSelectedRanges().

requirements.text: Reuse the verified public custom-function pattern by exposing a namespaced worksheet function that returns a mocked variable value by identifier, with matching TypeScript implementation and functions.json metadata.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f explicitly requires reuse of verified ps-excel-agent public-functions patterns.

[fact] ps-excel-agent origin/main c4900f696aeb1af3f78f377a6f61f35e28e1e59f files planningspace.integration.excel.ui/src/functions/functions.ts and functions.json contain matching exported public function implementations and metadata, including PSECANCELCALCULATIONS, ACCESS_TOKEN, AGENT_URL, TENANT, and CLIENT_ID.

[fact] Microsoft recommends a shared runtime for custom functions and documents manifest namespace, script, page, and metadata resources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/dev/add-ins/excel/custom-functions-overview.

[inference] A minimal function such as VARIABLEPOC.GETVARIABLE(identifier) demonstrates the requested pattern without coupling the supported task-pane/context-menu insertion flows to formula insertion. Unknown identifiers should return a clear Excel error or documented message.

requirements.text: Keep the POC self-contained: use no backend API, authentication, or external data service; use only the local static Angular HTTPS development host, and omit XLSM/VBA because no ready interaction requires a macro bridge.
evidence: [fact] User comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f says 'Use xlsm where helpful, no server or auth' and separately requires a local Angular HTTPS manifest target.

[conflict] A literal zero-server interpretation is incompatible with an Office task pane loading a local HTTPS web application; Microsoft states that add-in web files must be hosted: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/dev/add-ins/outlook/add-in-requirements.

[inference] The coherent bounded interpretation is no backend/application server and no authentication, while the Angular development server serves static local assets over HTTPS. Office.js directly supports the ready interactions, so XLSM/VBA adds no necessary capability and should be omitted under YAGNI.

requirements.text: Document setup, trusted HTTPS certificate creation, manifest sideloading, supported scenarios, the rejected drag scenario, and exact validation commands; provide focused automated tests and local build/manifest validation evidence.
evidence: [fact] The task is a runnable POC and user comment d5301b23c46949a0a1203adee1cef21f requires research findings and impossible-scenario explanations.

[fact] Microsoft documents office-addin-dev-certs for a trusted localhost certificate and local manifest sideloading: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/samples/officedev/office-add-in-samples/office-add-in-save-custom-settings/.

[fact] Global standard C:/Repos/development-agent-ecosystem/knowledge/managed/global/engineering-code-standards.md requires braces for all conditional bodies; TypeScript planning guidance requires type checking, linting, focused tests, and the actual build.

summary: [fact] The clean target branch is an empty POC repository, so all product behavior is missing. [fact] Current official contracts support local HTTPS Office add-ins, shared runtimes, ContextMenuCell ExecuteFunction commands, public custom functions, and one-or-many selected Excel ranges. [inference] Eight implementation areas are ready with no human-input dependency. [inference] Native drag of a task-pane DOM variable onto an Excel grid cell is rejected because Excel Office.js exposes no supported cross-surface drop target or target-cell contract; the POC will explain this and provide click and context-menu alternatives. humanReadable.title: Local Angular Excel variable-insertion proof of concept
humanReadable.objective: Build a self-contained Angular Excel add-in that shows 10 mock variables, inserts a chosen value into every selected cell by task-pane click or Excel right-click command, demonstrates the verified shared-runtime/public-function manifest pattern, and clearly explains why direct dragging from the task pane onto the worksheet grid is not a supported Office.js interaction.
